Job Description:

About bp and Brazil Upstream

bp is a global energy company with more than 50 years of operating history in Brazil, holding interests across multiple offshore blocks in the Santos, Campos and Espírito Santo basins. bp is committed to growing its upstream portfolio and establishing a material, advantaged production hub in Brazil.

In August 2025, bp announced its largest hydrocarbon discovery in 25 years at the Bumerangue block in the pre-salt Santos Basin, located approximately 404 km offshore Rio de Janeiro in a water depth of 2,372 meters. bp holds a 100% operated interest in the block, with Pré-Sal Petróleo S.A. (PPSA) as the production-sharing contract manager. Appraisal activities are planned to commence in 2027, with project development activities advancing in parallel.

The Bumerangue development is an important part of bp's broader Brazil Upstream portfolio. The E&S organisation therefore needs to support current and future operated activities across project development, drilling and related operational scopes, while also enabling collaboration with other bp businesses in Brazil where common E&S capability can contribute.

Role Purpose

The Environmental & Social (E&S) Lead will provide senior E&S leadership across bp's Upstream activities in Brazil, with initial focus on the Bumerangue development. The role will integrate environmental and social requirements across project development, drilling and future operated scopes, ensuring a coherent Brazil Upstream approach to E&S risk management, licensing, permitting, regulatory engagement and assurance.

The role will be responsible to guide and coordinate the Brazil Upstream E&S team, bringing together bp staff and contracted E&S resources under clear priorities, standards and accountabilities. It will act as the senior E&S focal point for Brazil Upstream and promote one coordinated bp work with IBAMA, ANP and other relevant authorities.

In addition to Upstream accountabilities, the role will provide E&S support to other bp businesses in Brazil, including GNA and NFX, as required, where shared expertise, regulatory knowledge or coordinated ways of working bring value. Businesses with dedicated E&S organisations remain responsible for their own core delivery.

This is a senior, permanent staff position based in Rio de Janeiro and reporting directly to the Project HSE & C Manager, Bumerangue Development.

Key Accountabilities

Brazil Upstream E&S Leadership & Integration

• Provide E&S leadership and oversight across all bp-operated Upstream activities in Brazil, covering projects, drilling and future operated developments.

• Lead and coordinate Brazil Upstream E&S staff and contracted resources across project, drilling, permitting and regulatory scopes, with clear priorities, accountabilities and performance expectations.

• Set portfolio E&S priorities, balance competing demands and call out material resource, capability or delivery gaps early.

• Act as the senior E&S focal point for Brazil Upstream and maintain one coordinated bp position with IBAMA, ANP and other relevant authorities.

• Drive consistency, quality and learning across work scopes through shared technical expertise, regulatory intelligence and lessons learned.

• Provide E&S support and technical leadership to GNA and NFX as required, using common capability without duplicating dedicated business resources.

Project Development, Licensing & Regulatory Delivery

• Lead identification and management of material E&S risks, commitments and opportunities across project development and drilling, ensuring requirements are integrated into business decisions, engineering, schedules and stage gates.

• Lead E&S integration with pre-FEED, FEED and EPCM contractors, including Environmental Design Basis requirements, environmental value improvement, BPEO/BAT assessments and relevant contractor specifications.

• Ensure EIA/RIMA and supporting biodiversity, marine, fisheries and socio-economic studies are appropriately scoped, procured and delivered to the required quality and schedule.

• Lead and coordinate Brazil Upstream environmental licensing and permitting strategies, including Bumerangue project and drilling scopes, through one coherent regulatory plan and roadmap.

• Build and maintain effective relationships with IBAMA, ANP and other relevant authorities and coordinate formal submissions, inspections, audits, technical reviews and responses to regulatory requests.

• Maintain traceability of E&S commitments from environmental and social studies through design, drilling, execution and operations readiness, and monitor regulatory developments that could affect bp activities in Brazil.

• Integrate interested party and social performance requirements into project and drilling plans, including engagement with affected communities, fisheries and municipalities, public consultation obligations and grievance mechanisms where required.

• Support climate and carbon considerations relevant to the portfolio, including Bumerangue reservoir CO2 implications, CO2 handling and emissions management.

Governance, Assurance & Delivery Management

• Represent E&S in relevant Brazil Upstream governance, assurance and investment forums and provide concise reporting on material risks, regulatory issues, resource constraints and mitigation actions.

• Ensure alignment with bp's HSSE & Social Performance Control Framework and maintain effective risk, commitment and action tracking with clear ownership and timely closure.

• Set E&S requirements for relevant contracts and provide proportionate oversight of ESIA and specialist environmental contractors, focusing on scope, quality, schedule, interfaces and regulatory defensibility.

• Maintain fit-for-purpose document and data controls for E&S studies, regulatory submissions, licence commitments and key decisions.

• Mentor and develop E&S resources in-country and deploy specialist expertise where needed to strengthen delivery across the portfolio.

Essential Experience & Qualifications

• Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is desirable.

• Highly skilled professional (minimum 15 years) of progressive E&S experience in the upstream oil and gas industry, including significant offshore project development and/or drilling experience.

• Demonstrated experience leading E&S teams and coordinating staff and contractor resources across multiple work scopes or assets.

• Track record of integrating E&S requirements into major capital projects, including design, FEED and EPC phases and management of complex environmental studies and contractors.

• Extensive hands-on experience with Brazilian environmental licensing for offshore oil and gas activities, including IBAMA engagement and EIA/RIMA processes, with strong working knowledge of relevant ANP requirements.

• Strong understanding of Brazil's federal environmental licensing framework and applicable international E&S standards, including IFC Performance Standards, Equator Principles and relevant ISO and bp requirements.

• Experience translating regulatory and E&S requirements into engineering deliverables, Environmental Design Basis documentation and contractor specifications.

• Fluent Portuguese and English, written and spoken, with strong leadership, communication and influencing skills. Direct regulatory communication in Portuguese is essential.

Desirable Experience & Qualifications

• Experience on pre-salt Santos Basin or deepwater Campos Basin developments and/or supporting a major deepwater project through FID into execution or operations readiness.

• Experience managing E&S requirements across both project development and drilling activities.

• Experience managing CO2-related environmental and regulatory considerations in upstream development.

• Registration with a relevant Brazilian professional body and familiarity with bp's HSSE & Social Performance framework are advantageous.

Why join us
At bp, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and high-reaching environment. We believe that our team is strengthened by diversity. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which everyone is respected and treated fairly.


There are many aspects of our employees’ lives that are meaningful, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life.

YOU NEVER met A PROBLEM YOU COULDN’T SOLVE

Belonging Matters Here

title: Quality Engineer Technician
description:
Job Title: Quality Engineering Technician

Job Summary


The Quality Engineering Technician supports various quality projects from inception through the testing phase. Responsibilities include assisting in the planning, development, and evaluation of new projects or processes. This role works collaboratively with other Quality Engineers and Process Engineering teams to ensure quality standards are met and to coordinate contributions for the successful completion of required quality projects.

Responsibilities


  • Ensure compliance with all legislative requirements in the facility’s location, including adherence to the Global Operating System Plays, OHSAS 18001:2007, ISO 14001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, and Linamar Quality Basics system standards.

  • Promote and demonstrate Linamar’s Core Values and Leadership Behaviors in all aspects of work.

  • Maintain a balance between customer, employee, and financial satisfaction by managing performance indicators aligned with Linamar’s Stepping Stool of Success Strategy.

  • Support and maintain lean initiatives in accordance with LPS system requirements, ensuring compliance with 5S standards within the department.

  • Develop instructions for capability studies and APQP activities, ensuring compliance with all PPAP requirements and documentation, including supplier submissions.

  • Champion the monthly issuance of corrective action requests (8D) and drive improvements where necessary.

  • Provide training and guidance to quality inspectors and other team members.

  • Lead team meetings, document and report on continuous quality improvement activities, and participate in continuous improvement programs.

  • Perform and document machine and process capability studies, ensuring regular calibrations and troubleshooting of inspection machines.

  • Ensure all activities comply with IATF 16949 procedures and systems.

  • Maintain a clean and organized quality assurance work area, including light maintenance responsibilities.

  • Stay current with developments in the field by maintaining certifications, engaging in continuous learning, and reading work-related publications.

  • Take direction from Quality Engineering to meet department goals and objectives.

  • Adhere to all health and safety regulations and procedures.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Academic/Educational Requirements


  • Applied Science degree or equivalent expertise gained through professional experience, training, or certifications.

  • Certified Quality Technician (CQT) certification preferred

Required Skills/Experience


  • Proficient in basic math (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division) using whole numbers, fractions, and decimals.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

  • Ability to meet company attendance standards and follow given instructions.

  • Experience in automotive quality assurance is required.

  • Prior experience in dealing with customers and suppliers at a management level.

  • Knowledge of IATF 16949 requirements and AIAG core tools.

  • Skilled in operating overhead cranes.

  • Strong data analysis skills, with working knowledge of Minitab, QC Calc, and MeasurLink.

  • CQE, CQA, and CQM certifications preferred.

  • Certification in machine programming (CMM, Gear CMMs, Shaft machines, etc.) is an advantage.

  • Previous experience in quality inspection/programming within a high-volume machine shop is preferred (3+ years).

  • Thorough knowledge of non-conforming material issues and the ability to make disposition decisions.

  • Skilled in interpreting machining drawings, diagrams, and callouts.

  • Proficient in using precise measurement tools such as micrometers, calipers, dial indicators, and angle finders.

  • Ability to evaluate and troubleshoot automated and mechanical gauges and tooling.

  • Proven ability to lead and train others in quality-related activities.

  • Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, including engineers, production operators, and quality control staff.


What Linamar Has to Offer


  • Competitive Compensation

  • Employee Benefits package includes but not limited to, Medical, Dental & Vision etc.

  • Opportunities for career advancement.

  • Community-based outreach supporting both local and global initiatives and charities.

  • Discounts for local vendors and events, including auto supplier discounts.

About Us


Linamar Corporation is a Canadian-founded global manufacturer, renowned for its advanced engineering and innovative product development across diverse industries and markets. Our journey started in 1966 under the visionary leadership of our founder, and today, we remain committed to cultivating a culture of innovation and collaboration.

With access to state-of-the-art tools and resources, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact alongside a team of driven and passionate professionals. Join us and be part of a company where innovation, collaboration, and growth are at the heart of everything we do.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, AWS EC2 Accelerator Team
description:
AWS builds the custom silicon and platforms that power the world's largest AI and machine learning workloads. We are looking for an exceptional Senior Technical Program Manager to drive the most complex, cross-organizational programs behind AWS's AI accelerators — Trainium and Inferentia.

In this role, you will own the end-to-end delivery of ambiguous, high-stakes programs that span silicon, hardware, software platforms, and ML frameworks. You will bring structure to ambiguity, drive alignment across many teams, surface and resolve the critical path, and hold a diverse set of stakeholders accountable to commitments. You will be the connective tissue that turns a portfolio of independent efforts into a coherent, on-time delivery — and the trusted voice leadership relies on for a clear-eyed view of status, risk, and the decisions that matter. This is a rare opportunity to shape how purpose-built AI infrastructure gets built and shipped at scale.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the planning and end-to-end delivery of large, cross-functional programs spanning silicon, hardware, software platforms, and ML frameworks — defining scope, milestones, dependencies, and the critical path.

- Drive alignment across many teams and leaders; establish mechanisms (planning, status, risk reviews) that keep a complex program moving and transparent.

- Proactively identify risks, dependencies, and bottlenecks; drive mitigations and force clarity on trade-offs before they become launch-blocking.

- Translate ambiguous, high-level goals into concrete plans with clear owners, dates, and success criteria.

- Communicate crisp status, risks, and decision asks to senior leadership; be the single source of truth for program health.

- Raise the bar on program management practices and mechanisms across the org, driving continuous improvement in how the team plans and executes.

A day in the life
You start the day scanning program dashboards and updating the critical path from a partner team. You run a cross-team sync to unblock a dependency between the hardware and software platform teams, then spend mid-morning pressure-testing a launch plan and pinning down owners and dates for the open risks. In the afternoon you drive a risk review, update the program's status narrative, and align stakeholders on a scope trade-off that protects the launch date. You close the day sending a crisp leadership update — where the program stands, the top risks, and the two decisions you need this week. Throughout, you are converting ambiguity into a clear, shared plan and holding the whole program accountable to it.

About the team
We are the platform organization behind AWS's Trainium and Inferentia accelerators — the custom AI chips that deliver industry-leading price-performance for training and inference. Our programs sit at the intersection of silicon, hardware, and large-scale distributed software. We operate at the frontier of AI infrastructure, where the programs we deliver directly shape the cost and speed of AI for customers worldwide. We value ownership, structured thinking, operational rigor, and a collaborative, high-trust culture where program managers and engineers succeed together.

Contract Management

Customer and Sales Support

title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period!

For more information about our benefits, see below!

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points

  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards

  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.

  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers

  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition

  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols

  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways

  • Working around animals, insects and termites

  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely

  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear

  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles

  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)

  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills

  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels

  • Customer-facing experience preferred

Pay Range

Hourly: $17.00 - $23.00

Why Choose Us?

A career with the Rentokil family of companies can be a professional trajectory filled with opportunity. We pride ourselves on being a world-class team that rewards high performance, and we love to promote from within. We offer competitive pay and many of our roles offer performance incentives.

description:

As part of the Seed Beauty family, we redefine what it means to innovate fast — and have fun doing it.

Position Summary
The Demand Planning & Master Data Coordinator supports demand forecasting and product master data management to ensure accurate planning, inventory availability, and operational excellence. This role maintains product master data across ERP systems, supports forecasting activities, and partners with Supply Chain, Sales, Marketing, Product Development, and Operations to ensure new product launches and ongoing planning activities are executed accurately and efficiently.

Key Responsibilities

Master Data Management
  • Create, maintain, and audit product master data within ERP and planning systems.
  • Manage SKU setup, product attributes, item hierarchies, units of measure, packaging configurations, and lifecycle changes.
  • Coordinate cross-functional data collection for new product introductions and product updates.
  • Ensure master data accuracy across ERP, planning, warehouse, and reporting systems.
  • Perform routine master data validation, cleansing, and quality audits.
  • Support data governance standards and documentation for product master records.
  • Partner with IT and Supply Chain teams to resolve master data issues affecting planning, purchasing, manufacturing, or order fulfillment.
Demand Planning
  • Provide support for weekly and monthly demand forecasting meetings
  • Assist with forecast maintenance within planning and ERP systems.
  • Prepare reporting and analysis for weekly demand review meetings and monthly S&OP processes.
  • Monitor inventory levels and identify potential stock shortages or excess inventory.
  • Support new product launch forecasting, SKU transitions, and product discontinuations.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Product Development, Regulatory, Finance, Operations, and Customer Service to support planning activities and product launches.
  • Assist in improving planning processes and data quality initiatives.
  • Develop reports and dashboards using Excel and Power BI or Tableau.
  • Support continuous improvement projects related to forecasting, inventory optimization, and data governance.
Qualifications
  • 2+ years of experience in master data, demand planning, supply chain, inventory management, or business analytics.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills (PivotTables, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH; Power Query is a plus).
  • Experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar.
  • Exposure to planning tools (SAP IBP, APO, Kinaxis, Blue Yonder, Anaplan) is preferred.
  • Understanding of product master data, SKU management, and data governance principles is a plus.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced beauty or consumer products environment.
  • Experience in beauty, cosmetics, apparel, or consumer packaged goods (CPG).
  • Familiarity with retailer requirements for Sephora, Ulta, Target, Walmart, Amazon, or similar channels.
  • Experience with Product Information Management (PIM) or Master Data Management (MDM) processes.
  • Knowledge of Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or basic data analytics.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field preferred
ColourPop offers a competitive benefits package including vacation time, health benefits, 401k + 100% match, paid holidays, product discounts and more. The hourly rate for this position is $29-$33 DOE (non-exempt) + discretionary annual bonus.

title: Principal Partner Value Engineer
description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role:

Elastic is seeking a Principal Partner Value Engineer to drive the economic blueprint of our strategic ecosystem. In this role, you will sit at the critical intersection of Elastic, our strategic Partners, and the ultimate End Customer. Your mission is two-fold: articulate and maximize Elastic’s value proposition to our partners, and co-create the partners' unified value proposition to the market.

We are looking for a high-impact professional with a deep background in partner ecosystems, a proven track record of value-based selling, and established partner relationships. This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in AMER. If you excel in dynamic environments, love building scalable frameworks, and are ready to be a change agent within a high-performing global team, we want to hear from you.

What You Will Be Doing:

  • Dual-Value Architecture: Co-develop and articulate the joint "Elastic + Partner" value proposition. Help partners understand the ROI of building on or with Elastic, while simultaneously helping partners position that combined value to their end customers.
  • Ecosystem Collaboration: Partner closely with Global Alliances, Channel Sales leaders, and partner account teams to identify, prioritize, and execute value delivery strategies for key regional and global partners.
  • Business Case and ROI Development: Lead joint business value reviews and create boardroom-quality business cases that quantify the economic benefits, total cost of ownership (TCO), and realized business impacts of Elastic-powered partner solutions.
  • Framework and Tool Creation: Help scale the Partner Value Engineering practice by creating repeatable frameworks, tools, and value calculators tailored specifically to different partner personas such as GSIs, MSSPs, and Cloud Hyperscalers.
  • Executive Presentation: Deliver compelling, high-impact presentations to partner executives and joint customers, acting as a trusted advisor on business transformation and optimization.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Work collaboratively with Product, Marketing, and Engineering teams to ensure partner feedback and unique ecosystem use cases are integrated into Elastic’s broader value strategy.
  • Enablement and Workshops: Conduct training sessions and workshops for both internal Elastic teams and partner organizations to elevate their discovery capabilities and understanding of value-based selling.

What You Bring:

  • Experience: 4+ years of experience in Value Engineering, Management Consulting, Partner Enablement, or a related customer or partner-facing strategic role.
  • Partner DNA: Proven experience working directly within or alongside partner ecosystems (GSIs, RSIs, MSPs, or Cloud Providers) with a strong network of existing partner relationships.
  • Value Selling Expertise: Expert-level knowledge of value-based selling methodologies (such as MEDDPICC, Challenger, or similar frameworks) and a demonstrated ability to build complex financial models and business cases.
  • Strategic and Analytical Skills: Strong analytical, financial acumen, and problem-solving skills. Ability to navigate ambiguity, project manage multiple workstreams, and act decisively under minimal supervision.
  • Communication Mastery: Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with a track record of influencing C-level executives and partner principals.
  • Location and Travel: Remote, based in North America. Willingness to travel as needed to meet with partners and account teams within your region.

Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People:

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.

We strive to have parity of benefits across regions, and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do.

  • Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary
  • Health coverage for you and your family in many locations
  • Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles
  • Generous number of vacation days each year
  • Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service
  • Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love
  • Embracing parenthood with a minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave

Different people approach problems differently. We need that. title: Founding GTM
description:
About Cozmo

Cozmo is the AI operating system for property claims. When a pipe bursts in someone's home at 2am, our agents answer the call, capture the loss, enter the claim into Xactimate and Cotality, dispatch the right contractor against SLA, chase acceptances before breach and draft the carrier-ready estimate from field photos. We run both halves of a claims operation: everything the customer touches and everything that happens behind the desk.

Our customers are restoration franchisors, TPAs and adjusting firms whose boards have told them to become AI-native and who have no way to do it themselves. Our anchor is one of the largest restoration franchisors in the US.

The role

You are hire one on the commercial team, selling next to a founder-CEO who currently closes everything himself. Your scorecard is closed revenue.

The market has a specific shape. There are a few hundred restoration franchisors, TPAs and adjusting firms in the US that matter. Their executives all know each other, they gather at a handful of conferences and most of them have been burned by software that promised automation and delivered a chatbot. Winning here means becoming a known person in claims within your first two quarters: on the floor at RESTORE and the Governor's Hurricane Conference, on the phone with franchise development VPs, in the room when a PE operating partner asks how the portfolio company gets AI-native before the exit.

You will take deals from cold call to signed SOW, run pilots alongside our forward deployed team and as we close, you write the playbook the next ten AEs run, and the founding title becomes a leadership seat you earned with a number.

You report to the CEO.

What you'll do

  • Own a number from month one: source, run and close enterprise deals with restoration franchisors, TPAs and adjusting firms
  • Cold call, cold email and work referrals into the claims executive network until the market knows Cozmo AI. Run complex sales: multiple stakeholders, operations and IT and franchise owners, pilots that convert to production contracts with gated expansion
  • Work conferences as pipeline engines, before, during and after the booth
  • Partner with the FDE team so what you sell is what goes live, and what goes live sells the expansion
  • Feed win-loss truth straight into positioning and product with both founders
  • Build the outbound machine: sequences, call scripts, battle cards, the CRM discipline the next hires inherit

What we look for

  • 1 to 6 years closing B2B deals with a verifiable number, or founder-level sales experience where you sold something that did not exist yet
  • Killer instinct on the phone. You pick it up without hesitating and you have call recordings or references that prove it
  • You can sell a technical product credibly: run your own demo, hold the room when an ops leader asks how the Xactimate entry works, know when to bring in an engineer
  • Fast learner in an unfamiliar industry. Nobody grows up in property damage; the ones who win learn the language in weeks
  • Evidence of hustle we can verify: quota history, a company you started, a territory you built from zero, a deal everyone said was dead
  • Thrives with direct founder feedback daily and a number visible to the whole company

Nice to have

  • Insurance, claims, restoration, field services or franchise sales
  • Selling b2b SAAS into operations buyers
  • Existing relationships in the TPA or restoration world

How we work

We are a small team racing incumbents with hundred times our headcount, and intensity is our only structural advantage, which means it is not a typical 9-5. If that schedule reads as a warning, this is the wrong role for you. If it reads as the environment where you finally get to run at full speed with people doing the same, keep reading.

Compensation

Base plus uncapped commission with a founding-level equity grant, weighted so that closing the plan changes your life twice: once in cash, once in ownership.

How to apply

No cover letter. Send three things to [email]:

  1. Your number, plainly: quota, attainment and the deal you are proudest of
  2. A 30 second loom video on how you would pick up the phone and pitch Cozmo, to the COO of a 200-location restoration franchisor
  3. The soonest date you can start

We respond to every real application within 48 hours. An exceptional answer to question 2 gets an interview regardless of resume.

Job Description

General Summary:

The Senior Director (non-MD) serves as a US Medical Affairs asset lead responsible for the strategic planning and execution of launch and lifecycle assets within the Vertex nephrology portfolio. This role provides scientific leadership and strategic direction across cross-functional teams, ensuring medical strategies are aligned with corporate objectives, patient needs, and the evolving US treatment landscape. The Senior Director is expected to build and lead a growing team of Medical Directors and Associate Medical Directors while serving as a trusted scientific partner to internal stakeholders and external thought leaders.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead the development, execution, and ongoing refinement of the US Medical Affairs strategic and operational plan for assigned nephrology asset(s), from pre-launch through lifecycle management.
  • Serve as the primary internal medical-scientific authority for the assigned asset, providing scientific interpretation of data (clinical trials, real-world evidence, published literature) and translating insights into actionable medical strategy.
  • Cultivate and maintain trusted scientific relationships with US nephrology thought leaders, academic investigators, and key external experts to inform medical strategy and support evidence generation.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Commercial, Market Access, HEOR, Regulatory, Clinical Development, and Corporate Communications to ensure aligned launch readiness and integrated execution in a matrix environment.
  • Drive the design and execution of medical evidence generation initiatives (e.g., investigator-sponsored research, advisory boards, medical education programs) aligned with the asset strategy and US medical needs.
  • Deliver and oversee the delivery of fair, balanced, and compliant scientific presentations and communications to healthcare professionals, payers, and other stakeholders.
  • Provide strategic medical input into promotional and non-promotional material review (CRC/MLR), ensuring all claims are scientifically substantiated and compliant with Vertex policies and US regulations.
  • Establish and track medical KPIs that demonstrate measurable impact on business outcomes and patient care; use scenario planning and market foresight to adapt strategies to a dynamic launch environment.
  • Ensure all activities are executed in full compliance with Vertex policies, US laws and regulations, GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable codes of practice.

Required Education Level

  • Terminal doctoral degree required (PhD, PharmD, MD, DO, or equivalent terminal scientific/clinical degree accepted).

Required Experience

Required Knowledge/Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to drive execution and deliver results in a highly matrixed, cross-functional environment.
  • Strong scientific knowledge of nephrology, immunology, or related therapeutic areas, including familiarity with the US treatment landscape, clinical trial design, and evidence generation.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to influence senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and external stakeholders.
  • Capacity to critically analyze and interpret complex scientific data and translate it into medical strategy.
  • Track record of planning, initiating, and completing high-impact projects within established timelines.

description:
About Us

Job Summary

The Systems Administrator is responsible for maintaining, supporting, and securing the organization’s IT infrastructure. This role provides technical support for user devices, servers, networks, Microsoft 365 services, enterprise applications, and endpoint management systems, while helping ensure systems remain reliable, secure, and operational. The position also supports system upgrades, software deployments, troubleshooting, documentation, and implementation of technology solutions that support business operations.

Role Description

  • Support and maintain Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) solutions for device configuration, software deployment, patching, and endpoint compliance.

  • Administer and support Windows servers, Active Directory, Microsoft 365 services, and related infrastructure.

  • Manage user accounts, permissions, access controls, groups, and system security settings.

  • Monitor system health, performance, backups, alerts, and security events.

  • Troubleshoot hardware, software, network, endpoint, and application issues.

  • Deploy software, updates, operating system patches, and configuration changes in accordance with established procedures.

  • Assist with cloud technologies, virtualization platforms, endpoint initiatives, infrastructure projects, and system migrations.

  • Maintain technical documentation, support procedures, asset information, and knowledge base articles.

  • Work with vendors, internal IT teams, and business stakeholders to resolve technical issues and implement new technologies.

  • Provide timely, professional technical support to end users while meeting service expectations and following escalation procedures.



Behaviors and Competencies

  • Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information, and can adapt communication style to the audience.

  • Time Management: Can generally use time effectively and is working towards improving task prioritization and deadline management.

  • Organization: Can prioritize daily tasks, manage personal workflow, and utilize basic tools to keep track of responsibilities.

  • Interpersonal Skills: Can communicate effectively, build relationships, and resolve conflicts with others in moderate situations.

  • Adaptability: Can adjust to changes in the work environment, manage multiple tasks, and effectively handle uncertainty.

  • Judgment: Can evaluate situations, identify patterns or implications, and decide on an appropriate course of action based on analysis and experience.

  • Initiative: Can identify opportunities for improvement, propose solutions, and take action without explicit instructions.

  • Collaboration: Can actively participate in team discussions, respect differing opinions, and collaborate with others to achieve common goals.

  • Digital Acumen: Can identify opportunities to use digital tools for improvement and propose digital solutions.

  • Willingness to Learn: Can actively seek out learning opportunities but may need guidance to apply new knowledge or skills effectively.

  • Technical Troubleshooting: Can identify complex technical issues, propose solutions, and take action to resolve them without explicit instructions.



Skill Level Requirements

  • Competence in managing and maintaining Active Directory, AWS, VMware, and Windows Server platforms. - Basic

  • Ability to read and understand cable matrices, structured cable routing experience, and basic understanding of IP addressing concepts for managing network and data center configurations. - Basic

  • Training or experience with Liebert/Emerson, APC suites, and hardware for uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). - Basic

  • Understanding of SAN storage concepts including zoning, LUN sizing, storage pools, RAID implementations, and volume configuration. - Basic

  • Experience with HP EVA, 3PAR, Pure Storage, and Cisco UCS storage solutions. - Basic



Other Requirements

  • Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience in IT systems administration.

  • 1–2 years of experience in systems administration or a related IT support role.

  • Experience with Windows Server, Active Directory, Microsoft 365, and networking.

  • Experience with a Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, such as Microsoft Intune, Ivanti, Workspace ONE, or similar endpoint management solutions.

  • Ability to work weekends and flexible hours

  • Ability to move or lift up to 50 lbs.

  • Certifications required: CompTIA A+, Network+, or Security+

  • Advanced certifications such as the following preferred: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, VMware VCP or equivalent virtualization certification, Microsoft 365, Windows Server, or endpoint management certifications

Preferred

  • Experience with scripting or automation tools such as PowerShell.

  • Familiarity with cybersecurity best practices, patch management, and endpoint compliance.

  • Experience supporting enterprise applications, mobile devices, printers, peripherals, and business technology systems.

  • Knowledge of virtualization technologies and cloud platforms such as Azure or AWS.

flexible spending.

GEOINT Analyst

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

  • Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
  • Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
  • Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Produce analytical products: Produce analytical products focused on foreign satellite communications spectrum usage and related operations.
  • Analyze and evaluate: Leverage SATCOM frequency bands to analyze satellite communication channels and optimize usage.
  • Assess performance: Utilize satellite monitoring capabilities to assess performance, including signal types, formatting, and modulation standards.
  • Analyze footprints: Analyze satellite beam footprints to evaluate coverage and optimize signal strength and clarity.
  • Assess effectiveness: Assess dish sizes and typical ground infrastructure to determine the effectiveness of satellite communication setups.
  • Track satellite signal sources: Apply geo-location capabilities to pinpoint and track satellite signal sources and assess their impact on operations
  • In-depth analysis: Conduct in-depth analysis of available intelink data, message traffic, GEOINT, SIGINT, and HUMINT to support satellite communication assessments.
  • Interpret and correlate intelligence: Use analytic tools and methodologies to interpret and correlate intelligence from various sources in satellite communications.
  • Provide actionable insights: Provide actionable insights into signal integrity, reliability, and performance, using data from satellite systems and communication infrastructures.
  • Collaborate across teams: Collaborate with other teams to ensure secure and efficient use of satellite communications in complex operational environments.

Work Environment:

  • Location: On-site
  • Travel Requirements: Minimal 0-20%
  • Working Hours: Standard

Qualifications:

Required:

  • Clearance: Active TS/SCI

title: Quality Assurance Coordinator
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

The Quality Coordinator is a senior individual contributor role responsible for fleet wide governance and quality assurance of Incident Management and Process/Product Nonconformance programs, while also owning site specific quality process execution and improvement activities at the Invenergy Central Machine Shop.


This role serves as the Quality system steward for incident investigations and nonconformance governance across the fleet, ensuring consistent application of risk based rigor, investigation quality, and corrective action effectiveness in accordance with Invenergy policy and procedures. In parallel, the role provides hands on quality process leadership at the Central Machine Shop, supporting manufacturing, repair, inspection, and continuous improvement activities.


The Quality Coordinator operates as a technical authority, governance facilitator, and cross functional partner, not as a people manager.

  • Provide fleet wide governance oversight for Incident Management and Process/Product Nonconformance programs, ensuring consistent application of Invenergy policies, risk classification criteria, investigation rigor, and closure expectations across all sites.
  • Serve as the Quality authority for investigation governance, reviewing incidents, near misses, and nonconformances to confirm:
  • Act as the Quality representative and facilitator for enterprise governance forums (e.g., Nonconformance Risk Review Committee), including convening reviews, confirming risk classifications, validating investigation scope and rigor, and assessing corrective action adequacy and scalability.
  • Ensure clear governance handoff between Nonconformance Management and Incident Management when Serious Injury or Fatality potential (SIFp) criteria are identified, avoiding duplication and maintaining procedural alignment.
  • Maintain Intelex as the authoritative system of record, enforcing discipline in documentation, approvals, rationale, corrective actions, and evidence to ensure transparency, traceability, and audit readiness.
  • Analyze fleet wide trends, repeat issues, and systemic weaknesses related to incidents and nonconformances; elevate insights and recommendations to the Director of Quality to support continuous improvement and preventive actions.
  • Own site level quality process execution at the Central Machine Shop, including identification and documentation of process or product deviations, support of investigations, and verification of corrective action completion for shop specific issues.
  • Partner with Machine Shop leadership, Engineering, Operations, and EHS to improve process consistency, inspection effectiveness, and defect prevention, translating fleet level lessons learned into practical local process improvements.
  • Provide technical guidance and coaching to investigation owners and contributors across the fleet on risk based thinking, governance expectations, and documentation quality, without assuming execution ownership or people management responsibility.
  • Up to 20% travel may be required.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned

Qualifications & Experience

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations, or related discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in quality, operations, engineering, incident management, manufacturing, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience with:
    • Incident or event investigation frameworks
    • Nonconformance / deviation management
    • Risk‑based governance models
  • Strong analytical, documentation, and facilitation skills.
  • Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Preferred:

  • Experience with Intelex or similar ESHQ/ Quality Systems
  • Exposure to SIFp‑based incident classification.
  • Manufacturing, repair, or industrial shop experience.
  • Familiarity with causal analysis methods (e.g., Cause Mapping, 5‑Why).
  • System‑level thinker with strong governance discipline
  • Comfortable influencing across sites without direct authority
  • Detail‑oriented, audit‑ready, and process‑driven
  • Clear, confident communicator who can challenge constructively

Base Pay

$80,000.00 - $90,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 10% - 25%

The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.

In addition to base pay, the total annual compensation package may also include eligibility to participate in our bonus program(s) which are designed to reward individual and company performance. Your recruiter can share more about bonus eligibility for this position during the hiring process.

Invenergy offers a variety of other benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k, profit sharing, paid time off, etc.

Senior TPRM Consultant (Partner Engagements)

Location: 1540 Broadway, New York, NY 10036
Department: Corporate Controllership – Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM)

Position Summary:

The Senior TPRM Consultant is responsible for supporting the development and management of the TPRM Program framework, specifically for the sales partner ecosystem (e.g., solution partners, system integrators, resellers and distributors). This role sits at the intersection of risk management, sales, legal, and sales operations — and requires someone who can independently drive risk conversations forward, not simply administer a process. Success in this role depends on your ability to lead — setting the agenda, holding partners and internal stakeholders accountable to timelines, and driving issues to closure.

The role supports the design, maintenance, and enforcement of TPRM policy, standards, and governance. In close partnership with risk domain leads and cross-functional stakeholders, this role helps advance program maturity, support regulatory alignment, and strengthen third-party risk practices across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage the TPRM governance committees, including preparing materials and strategizing focused agendas that drive risk identification, mitigation, and oversight.
  • Set the TPRM governance framework by defining roles and responsibilities to ensure appropriate oversight of third-party engagements and manage associated risks; and enhancing risk treatment / risk acceptance processes.
  • Determine and establish program metrics, including key performance and risk indicators (KPIs/KRIs) to enable effective oversight of the TPRM program.
  • Maintain TPRM policies, procedures, and governance documentation to reflect regulatory changes and evolving industry standards.
  • Lead the management and oversight of third-party risk management control requirements and framework.
  • Support the development of board and senior management materials that clearly communicate TPRM objectives, priorities, and program health using metrics and thresholds.
  • Support the implementation and continuous enhancement of Adobe’s TPRM governance framework to strengthen risk management across all third-party relationships.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams (Legal, Sales, Sales Ops, Compliance, Procurement, Security) to ensure consistent application of TPRM policies and risk requirements.
  • Collaborate with the TPRM Training & Awareness Manager to design and deliver training and awareness materials that reinforce policy compliance and third-party lifecycle management.
  • Contribute to the ongoing enhancement of TPRM tools, technology, and workflows (e.g., GRC platforms).

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Compliance, or a related field.
  • 5–7 years of experience in third-party risk management, governance, compliance, or related oversight roles with at minimum, 2 years of experience driving and managing projects or programs.
  • Strong understanding of third-party risk management and risk management fundamentals.
  • Familiarity with regulatory and security frameworks (e.g., FCPA / UK Bribery Act, GDPR, NIST RMF, ISO 27001) and third-party risk management tools.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.

When a pipe bursts in someone's home at 2am, our agents answer the call, capture the loss, enter the claim into Xactimate and Cotality, dispatch the right contractor against SLA, chase acceptances before breach and draft the carrier-ready estimate from field photos. We run both halves of a claims operation: everything the customer touches and everything that happens behind the desk.

Our customers are restoration franchisors, TPAs and adjusting firms whose boards have told them to become AI-native and who have no way to do it themselves. Our anchor is one of the largest restoration franchisors in the US.

The role

A claim is a hostile engineering environment. The data lives in Xactimate files, carrier portals, Zendesk queues, voicemails and photos of wet drywall. The workflows were designed twenty years ago and enforced by franchise agreements. SLAs are measured in minutes and breaches cost real money. Your job is to walk into that environment, reason from first principles about what the system should be, then build agents that run it in production.

You will spend part of your time inside customer operations, part of it writing code that becomes the platform. The distance between "I saw a dispatcher waste an hour on this" and "an agent now does it" should be days, and you own the whole distance.

You report to the CTO and work directly with both founders.

What you'll do

  • Deploy into enterprise claims operations and own technical outcomes end to end
  • Build production agent systems: prompt architectures, tool use, routing, evals, fallbacks, the glue between LLMs and systems that were never meant to have APIs
  • Reverse engineer legacy claims software and make it programmable
  • Design the data layer as you go. Every claim we touch generates hundreds of structured data points, and the pipelines you build become the moat
  • Ship during live go-lives with hard dates and executives watching, including hurricane season surges where volume triples overnight
  • Convert field solutions into platform primitives so each deployment is faster than the last

What we look for

  • Exceptional CS fundamentals from a top program, or the self-taught equivalent with proof. We care about the caliber of your thinking and we will test it directly
  • 0 to 4 years of experience. New grads welcome if your work says more than your resume
  • You build fast and deep: strong in Python or TypeScript, comfortable across the stack, able to go from empty repo to production system alone
  • Hands-on LLM engineering: you have built agent systems, written evals and know where models break, beyond calling an API in a notebook
  • First-principles reasoning. When the standard workflow is wrong you notice, and you can defend the redesign to the person who has run it for twenty years
  • Evidence of ambition we can inspect: research, a startup, open source, competition results, something shipped that people use
  • You want to be around customers. The best FDEs treat the deployment as the interesting part

Nice to have

  • Voice AI, telephony or real-time systems
  • Insurance, claims or field services domain exposure
  • Winning record in competitive programming, olympiads or research

How we work

We work almost six days a week, in person in New York, and go-live weeks take the seventh day too. We say this plainly because intensity is our structural advantage against incumbents with a hundred times our headcount, and because the engineers we want read this section and relax. This is the environment where nobody tells you to slow down.

Compensation

Competitive salary plus founding-level equity, weighted toward equity because we want owners, plus relocation to NYC if required.

How to apply

No cover letter. Send three things to me:

  1. The hardest technical thing you have built, with code or artifact we can inspect
  2. A first-principles answer, under 60 seconds as a loom/Vimeo video, to: an agent must enter a water damage estimate into Xact from a phone call transcript and 40 photos. What breaks first, and how do you design around it?
  3. The soonest date you can start

We respond to every real application within 48 hours. Strong answers to question 2 get an interview regardless of resume.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

As the Senior Director, GTM Executive Communications, Strategy & Operations, you will lead the organization tasked with transforming Elastic's go-to-market strategy into clear, compelling, and actionable communications that enable execution across our global revenue organization.

Reporting to Global Revenue Operations, you will serve as the strategic communications partner to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) and Revenue Operations Team, ensuring business priorities are translated into communications, programs, and experiences that align leaders, equip managers, and enable the field to execute with confidence.

Your organization has three main areas of focus. They are Executive Communications, Communications Strategy and Operations, and Executive Engagement Programs. Collectively, these functions establish the narrative, governance, and operating model that drive consistent execution across the GTM organization.

This role extends beyond traditional internal communications. You will create the GTM narrative. You will update communications with AI and scalable operations. You will manage executive programs. These programs will improve customer relationships and accelerate business results.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead GTM Narrative & Communications Strategy

  • Define the communications strategy that supports Elastic's GTM priorities and business objectives.

  • Translate complex ideas into simple and clear messages. These ideas include annual planning, sales strategies, compensation, launching products, changes in the organization, and operational strategy.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the CRO and executive executive team team on strategic communications and change management.

Drive Executive Communications & Operations

  • Lead executive messaging, presentations, keynotes, management communications, and field-facing content for the CRO and GTM management team team.

  • Establish rules for communication and editorial standards. Create content operations and workflows that use AI. Set up measurements to improve clarity, consistency, and adoption in the organization.

  • Build scalable communications frameworks, toolkits, and manager enablement that reinforce strategic priorities and drive execution.

Lead Executive Engagement Programs

  • Provide strategic oversight for Elastic's executive engagement portfolio. This portfolio includes the Customer Innovation Center (CIC), the Executive Sponsorship Program, the Net Promoter Score (NPS), and future executive initiatives.

  • Lead program leaders responsible for delivering consistent, measurable executive experiences that strengthen customer relationships and support GTM growth.

  • Establish governance, success metrics, and executive reporting to measure program impact and identify opportunities for innovation.

Enable Organizational Change

  • Create communication strategies. These strategies will support changes in the organization. They will also update the operating model and important go-to-market initiatives.

  • Partner across Revenue Operations, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Product, Legal, and People to ensure coordinated, timely, and effective communications that drive adoption and business impact.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of management experience in Executive Communications, Revenue Operations, GTM Strategy, Sales Operations, Chief of Staff, GTM Enablement, or Strategic Communications, including experience leading high-performing teams.

  • Proven ability to translate complex business strategy into compelling executive narratives that influence decision-making and accelerate field execution.

  • You should have a remarkable executive presence. You also need solid skills in technical writing and stakeholder management. Experience working directly with senior executives is required.

  • You should have a deep knowledge of SaaS go-to-market operating models. This includes annual planning, sales motions, territory strategy, forecasting, and making changes in the organization.

  • Experience in building communication operations that can grow. Knowledge of governance and workflows that use AI for content. Involvement in executive programs in a fast-growing B2B environment.

title: IVI Hardware Architecture - Technical Specialist
description:
Ford’s Electric Vehicles, Digital and Design (EVDD) team is charged with delivering the company’s vision of a fully electric transportation future. EVDD is customer-obsessed, entrepreneurial, and data-driven and is dedicated to delivering industry-leading customer experience for electric vehicle buyers and owners. You’ll join an agile team of doers pioneering our EV future by working collaboratively, staying focused on only what matters, and delivering excellence day in and day out. Join us to make positive change by helping build a better world where every person is free to move and pursue their dreams.

In this position...

The IVI Hardware Architecture - Technical Specialist is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role responsible for the hardware architecture, technical direction, and engineering maturity of Ford in-vehicle infotainment electronic control units and their key electrical interfaces. The Technical Specialist provides deep expertise in high-performance automotive compute hardware, including power delivery, processing, memory, storage, display, connectivity, thermal, and high-speed vehicle-network interfaces.

The role defines and governs hardware requirements, architecture decisions, design reviews, validation expectations, and technical issue resolution for IVI hardware programs. Working with Ford engineering teams, suppliers, systems engineering, software, validation, quality, and vehicle electrical architecture teams, this individual ensures IVI hardware designs are robust, manufacturable, validated, and ready for production, and serves as the final technical sign-off for hardware design and pre- and post-test validation before release.

The Technical Specialist is expected to interpret schematics and PCB layouts, evaluate circuit and system behavior, support hands-on laboratory investigation when needed, and lead resolution of complex hardware and cross-domain issues from concept through launch and post-launch quality support.

What you'll do...

  • Own the hardware architecture and technical direction for IVI ECU platforms and their interfaces to displays, vehicle networks, power modes, connectivity modules, and associated vehicle electronics.

  • Serve as the final technical sign-off for IVI ECU hardware release, approving hardware design and pre- and post-test validation before production.

  • Define hardware-level and system-level requirements, interface specifications, architecture principles, design constraints, and validation methods for internal teams and external suppliers.

  • Lead technical reviews of schematics, PCB layouts, component selections, power architectures, thermal approaches, high-speed interfaces, and design-validation evidence.

  • Evaluate hardware capability and margin for processor, memory, storage, display, connectivity, power, thermal, and network workloads.

  • Provide expert technical guidance for ECU boot, wake/sleep, power sequencing, network management, reliability, performance, and hardware/software interaction.

  • Lead or support hands-on lab investigations of complex board-, ECU-, and vehicle-level failures using appropriate electrical, thermal, network, and diagnostic tools.

  • Review WCCA strategy and results, identify design risks, and drive mitigations with responsible design and supplier teams.

  • Define and approve hardware validation, integration, robustness, EMC, environmental, and production-readiness expectations.

  • Lead technical root-cause investigations and corrective actions for significant hardware and cross-functional issues using structured methods such as 8D, fishbone, fault-tree analysis, and FMEA.

  • Provide technical leadership to suppliers and internal design teams; assess design maturity and provide technical recommendations for gateway, milestone, and release decisions.

  • Ensure IVI hardware designs support applicable cybersecurity, functional-safety, EMC, environmental, regulatory, manufacturing, and service requirements.

You'll have...

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • 10+ years of experience in automotive electronic hardware design, design and release, or electrical/electronic architecture, including work on cockpit, infotainment, connectivity, modem, gateway, or other complex vehicle ECU hardware.

  • Demonstrated experience defining hardware architecture, electrical and system requirements, interface specifications, and validation strategies for automotive ECUs, and leading technical design reviews through production.

  • Strong ability to read, interpret, and technically review schematics, PCB layouts, data sheets, and validation reports, with deep knowledge of high-performance compute ECU hardware — processors/SoCs, memory and storage interfaces (LPDDR, eMMC/UFS), power delivery and sequencing, thermal management, signal/power integrity, and high-speed vehicle interfaces (Automotive Ethernet, CAN/CAN FD, LIN, USB, PCIe, display).

  • Proven experience resolving complex hardware issues at board, module, and vehicle-system levels using structured problem-solving methods (8D, fishbone, fault-tree, FMEA), with strong communication skills across internal teams, suppliers, and cross-functional stakeholders.

Even better, you may have...

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • 15+ years of relevant automotive electronics experience, including recognized technical leadership in ECU hardware architecture, design and release, or electronics development.

  • Experience serving as the technical lead or technical authority for an automotive ECU from concept through production launch and post-launch quality support.

  • Deep expertise in one or more IVI hardware domains, such as power management (PMICs, DC/DC converters, load switches, sequencing, low-power modes); high-speed digital design, signal integrity, power integrity, clocking, reset, and EMI/EMC mitigation; SoC and memory subsystem integration; or thermal design, characterization, and derating for high-performance compute ECUs.

  • Deep expertise in one or more IVI interface domains, such as display, touch, camera, and video hardware interfaces; Automotive Ethernet, network switch, gateway, and diagnostic hardware; or wireless and connectivity-module integration, including cellular, GNSS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, antenna, and RF coexistence considerations.

  • Experience performing, reviewing, or driving closure of Worst-Case Circuit Analysis, tolerance analysis, derating analysis, and related electrical design-risk assessments, as well as automotive EMC/EMI design, test planning, test execution, and corrective-action development.

  • Knowledge of automotive cybersecurity and functional-safety processes as applied to connected electronic modules (ISO/SAE 21434, ISO 26262), along with automotive product-development and quality processes such as APQP, PPAP, DFMEA, PFMEA, DV/PV, supplier technical reviews, and launch readiness; familiarity with Ford processes and tools such as GPDS is a plus.

  • Proficiency with relevant lab and engineering tools (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, spectrum/network/power analyzers, electronic loads, thermal cameras, environmental chambers, CAN/Ethernet analysis tools), electrical simulation tools (LTspice, MATLAB/Simulink, Mathcad, HyperLynx, SI/PI tools), PCB design, fabrication, assembly, manufacturing test, and DFM/DFT practices, and basic scripting or automation (Python, MATLAB, or similar) for lab automation, data reduction, and test reporting.

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:

• Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage

title: Materials Planner-Buyer
description:

This role is responsible for ensuring the timely and cost-effective procurement of raw materials to support uninterrupted production within a specialty chemical manufacturing environment. This position is located onsite at our specialty chemical production plant office at 4700 S. Central in Forest View, IL. This role is non-exempt with a Monday-Friday work schedule and reports to the Purchasing Director.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following.

  • Evaluate the daily raw material requirements report, place orders with the appropriate suppliers in a timely manner to ensure sufficient inventory for production.
  • Proactively identifies supply risks and communicate any supply issues with scheduling, production, and department management.
  • Maintain a positive business relationship with suppliers which include communication with key contacts, pricing and supply discussions, identifying and disseminating new product opportunities to the appropriate people, as well as handling the resolution of quality and supply issues. This includes meeting with supplier’s representatives on a regular basis.
  • Seek alternate source of suppliers and solicit samples as needed for evaluation by R&D.
  • Responsible for miscellaneous internal PO process.
  • Using database reports to review status of open purchase orders and follow up internally or externally with vendors as necessary. Enter PO’s into database.
  • Maintain the appropriate vendor files including quotations, contacts, current costs, IVR, etc. in the database.
  • Negotiate pricing and freight costs for select raw materials within department guidelines.
  • Work with various internal departments such as production, scheduling, customer service, maintenance, engineering and accounting to communicate with & resolve purchasing related issues.
  • Responsible for all purchasing related documents, organization, and filing. Accurately prepare receiving paperwork and forward to AP in a timely manner.
  • Attend the daily morning production meeting.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, and ABILITIES

At a minimum, high school diploma or GED is required. Some college business or supply chain coursework is beneficial. Minimum of two years of purchasing and materials planning work experience is required; experience in a manufacturing environment is preferred and experience in chemicals purchasing is a big plus.

  • Ability to communicate professionally, confidently and effectively with suppliers and vendors to meet company’s needs.
  • Strong negotiation and problem solving skills. Demonstrate persistence and tact with vendors to ensure that Daubert’s supply needs are met within our timeframes so as to not disrupt production.
  • Detail oriented with strong organizational skills.
  • Self-starter with ability to work independently and efficiently once trained.
  • Ability to analyze reports and make decisions on inventory and purchasing decisions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • Consistent & punctual attendance is required due to operational requirements.
  • PC proficiency is required; Microsoft Suite (Outlook, word, excel), plus .pdf creation, file management, internet navigation and placement of online orders experience is required.
  • Strong mathematical and calculation skills are essential.
  • Ability to learn current database of AS400 then transition into learning the new ERP database, MS Dynamics or D365, for all daily work.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Pay range $28-$35 per hour
  • BCBS of Illinois Medical & Dental, plus Vision Service Plan.
  • 401(k) Savings Plan + generous bi-weekly Company Match
  • Paid time off, plus 11 annual Holidays
  • Disability, Family, & Military Leave
  • Life Insurance (Whole & Term), Identity Protection and more!

Relocation assistance is not available. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

Maintains and demonstrates an in-depth knowledge of nursing principles, practices, standards, and techniques and applies this knowledge in accordance with St. Charles Health System policies and procedures and within laws and regulations governing nursing practice in the State of Oregon.

Participates in creating intentional relationships and demonstrates focused attitudes and behaviors that enhance the care experience.

title: Remote Senior Software Engineer (Backend Focus)
description:
We are seeking an exceptionally skilled, senior-level Senior Software Engineer for a strictly backend-focused role. Front-end-heavy candidates are not the target profile for this position. This role requires an expert engineer who can drive backend engineering initiatives for large-scale, complex applications. You will serve as a technical anchor, providing architectural direction and cross-domain troubleshooting expertise to ensure the successful delivery of highly scalable, distributed, cloud-native backend systems.

Requirements & Qualifications (Must Have)

  • Expert-level Java programming experience, including hands-on development of testable code, a clear understanding of the SDLC, and the ability to write efficient unit test cases and automation test scripts.
  • Microservices experience with a strong backend focus.
  • Backend systems experience, including work on large-scale, complex applications.
  • Experience in the payments industry or building payment applications.
  • Distributed systems and scalable application development experience, including cloud-native applications, algorithms, logging frameworks, scaling, and UML principles.
  • Expert in SOAP/REST communication and the usage of test harnesses.
  • Experience working with and possessing knowledge of merge methodologies using version control systems like Git, GitLab, and BitBucket.
  • Familiarity or experience with test automation frameworks (such as Cypress.io, TestRail, Selenium, and Jenkins) as applied within a backend or full-cycle engineering context.

Desirable Skills (Nice to Have)

  • AI experience.
  • Risk and compliance experience.
  • Database management and data migration experience, including work with specific database technologies like Oracle, RDS, and DynamoDB.
  • Cloud platform experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP.

Interview Process

  • Two interview rounds are planned, with at least one live, shared-screen coding assessment.

Major Duties & Responsibilities

  • Technical Direction & Architecture: Lead and give technical direction to fellow engineers while authoring extensive architecture and design documents utilizing distributed system design, algorithms, logging frameworks, scaling, and microservices principles.
  • Backend Code Development: Write high-quality, testable, expert-level Java code within a backend-focused full-cycle engineering framework, maintaining a clear understanding of the complete SDLC.
  • Cloud & Payments Application Engineering: Design, build, and deploy scalable cloud-native applications inside public cloud infrastructures, specifically optimizing core backend infrastructure for the payments industry.
  • Database & Migration Management: Administer and integrate applications with enterprise database technologies, supporting backend data migration initiatives and utilizing expert-level communication protocols.
  • Version Control Tracking: Oversee and manage codebase integration using precise merge methodologies across version control platforms like Git, GitLab, BitBucket, etc.
  • Cross-Domain Troubleshooting: Deliver excellent troubleshooting and issue resolution skills, demonstrating the capacity to quickly isolate and debug complex technical issues even when they occur in areas outside of your immediate domain.
